question.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}4{e}^{x}-5 & >0 \\ 4{e}^{x} & >5 \\ {e}^{x} & >\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x}) & >\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{5}{4}) \\ x & >\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡4.\end{aligned}
$$
